WMT.rationale: Walmart is the world's largest retailer with dominant scale, strong e-commerce momentum (24% YoY growth, $150B+ in FY2026), and a growing high-margin advertising business (46% growth). However, the investment case is tempered by several factors. Fundamentally, Q1 FY2027 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +7.3%, EPS +19.6%) but QoQ metrics were soft (EPS -13%, operating cash flow -47.9%), and the TTM picture is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps. Net margins remain structurally thin at ~3.1-3.2%, and operating cash flow has been volatile. The balance sheet is healthy with $100.7B equity. On valuation, the stock has pulled back meaningfully from its May 2026 highs (~$135 to $112, a ~17% decline), and the P/E has compressed from ~54x to ~39x — now near the low end of its 365-day range (37.6-55.4). However, 39x P/E for a ~3% net margin retailer with mid-single-digit revenue growth is still a significant premium to the broader market and retail peers (~18-25x). The tailored fair P/E analysis from Simply Wall St suggests ~38.4x is roughly fair, implying limited upside from current levels. Near-term catalysts are mixed: Q2 earnings on Aug 20 could re-rate the stock, and JPMorgan has it as a top idea with a $137 target (~25% upside). However, Cleveland Research flagged slowing U.S. comparable sales, and the July 1 sell-off (-4.5%) on that report shows the stock is sensitive to any negative data points at this valuation. Chinese food safety regulatory scrutiny on Sam's Club adds a modest risk. The stock is mildly attractive — a quality franchise at a more reasonable valuation than recent history, but not cheap enough to be compelling given thin margins and macro headwinds (rising 10Y yields at 4.54%, elevated oil prices until recent decline, consumer spending caution).
